newsitem.title: FRANCE: French maize harvest in full swing after rain.
newsitem.headline: French maize harvest in full swing after rain.

text.p: Maize combining is in full swing in France's southwest after rain delayed the start of the bulk of the harvest by about two weeks, crop analysts said on Monday.
But harvesting delays have created some backlog at silos, where the grain is waiting to be dried, they said.
"There are no major storage problems. But the situation is getting a little tight in some silos as the crop was late," one analyst for the local ONIC office in Bordeaux told Reuters.

In the Aquitaine region, where most of France's maize is produced, combining of early variety maize started in September in the Haute-Landes region but the bulk of the harvest got under way only last week.
The harvest is now 25-30 percent complete in the region and may be over by the end of November if it does not rain, analysts said.
Local ONIC officials said they were maintaining their pre-harvest forecast of 1996 yields at the 1993 record of 8.6 tonnes per hectare after 8.0 tonnes last year.
Area is expected to rise 4.2 percent to 370,000 hectares.
In the Midi-Pyrenees region combining also started last week. Local ONIC officials predicted the harvest may be 50 percent complete by the end of this week.
Early results suggested yields may rise to between 7.8 and 8.0 tonnes per hectare from 7.2 tonnes last year, they said.
Area is expected to increase by 4.6 percent to 225,000 hectares.
In eastern France the first cuttings started in late September but farmers stopped combining when they realised the grain had not fully matured.
The harvest resumed last week, with combining now 30 to 40 percent complete.
Local yields are expected to jump to 9.5 tonnes from 8.9 tonnes last year and area to 126,000 hectares from 115,000.
The French maize growers association AGPM has put the 1996 national crop at 13.8 million tonnes, up one million from 1995.
